name: binding-price
description: The market of ledger row #13, executed: privacy is bought, binding is not — and here is the equation that makes them one coin. The identity: a reveal's pass probability exceeds 1/2 by exactly half the verifier marginal's polarization along the announced state — Tr[|a><a| rho] = (1 + a.r)/2 — so every unit of binding slack IS a unit of concealment loss (binding slack = TV distance from I/2, one-to-one). The flat supply: across the promisor's entire HJW strategy space — random bases, the tetrahedral decomposition, mixed-member ensembles — the verifier's marginal stays I/2 and the reveal stays exactly 1/2: no decomposition moves it at any price, witnessed by machine (an asserted impossibility without a witness is marketing). The sellable goods keep their price list: entangled concealment T=0, tamper detection 1-(3/4)^m, the pad economy. The classical frontier ships as one parameter with two prices. The checker enforces the market laws; the renderer refuses illegal ledgers.
